overview.description: LegacyHQ uses a three-tier token architecture to create a scalable, maintainable, and themeable design system while minimizing duplicate meanings.

tiers.name: Primitive Tokens
rules: Primitive tokens contain raw values only.
Primitive tokens must not represent intent.
Components must never consume primitive tokens directly.

tiers.name: Semantic Tokens
rules: Semantic tokens should be the primary tokens consumed throughout the system.
Semantic tokens map to primitive tokens.
New semantic tokens should only be created when a new meaning is introduced.

tiers.name: Component Tokens
rules: Component tokens are exceptions, not defaults.
Component tokens should generally alias semantic tokens.
Component tokens should only exist when a component requires independent control, theming, or behavior.

componentTokenCreationRule.description: Before creating a component token, determine whether the semantic layer already expresses the needed meaning.
steps: Determine whether a semantic token already expresses the same meaning.
Reuse the semantic token whenever possible.
Create a component token only when the semantic layer cannot adequately express the requirement.

ifEquivalentSemanticTokenExists.rule: If an equivalent semantic token exists, do not create a new component token.

avoidExample.allowedOnlyWhen: There is a documented need for independent control.

interactionStateVocabulary.summary: One canonical word per interaction state, used identically in Figma variable names, generated CSS custom properties, component variant axes, and the data-force-state escape hatch. Unified across Figma and code together - there is no longer a past-participle form anywhere.
rules: Use the bare-verb form: hover (not hover), press (not press), focus (not focus).
A token whose name ends in a state uses exactly one of these words, e.g. color.background.neutral.overlay.hover / .press, color.border.focus, color.border.selected.
The Storybook data-force-state escape hatch takes the same vocabulary: data-force-state="hover" | "focus" | "press". It is documentation-only and never part of a public API.
notCovered: CSS pseudo-classes are browser primitives and keep their own spelling: :hover, :focus-visible, :active. Only our own names follow this vocabulary - :active is the platform selector that implements the press state.
ARIA attributes keep their spec spelling: aria-press, aria-selected, aria-disabled, aria-busy.
ProgressIndicator step progress uses an unrelated data-state="active|complete|incomplete" axis - that is step position, not interaction, and is out of scope for this vocabulary.
Grammatical English prose in comments and docs is unaffected ("tinted while hovered" is prose, not an identifier).

antiPatterns: Component tokens that mirror existing semantic tokens.
Component tokens that reference primitive values directly.
Creating tokens for a single isolated use case.
Creating semantic tokens that differ only by component name.

questions: Can an existing semantic token be reused?
Will multiple components share this meaning?
Does the token represent meaning or implementation?
decisionFramework.defaultDecision: If a semantic token already expresses the meaning, reuse it.
decisionFramework.principle: When in doubt, prefer fewer tokens with clearer intent.

enforcement.description: This governance doc is a convention, not a guarantee. Raw-value regressions in component CSS are caught mechanically by stylelint, not by review alone.

gated: padding, margin, and gap (and their longhands)

notGated.reason: These frequently require geometric arithmetic (calc(), negative offsets) that doesn't map onto the token scale; gating them produced false positives against legitimate layout math.

scope.escapeHatch: A raw value can still pass via an inline `stylelint-disable-next-line scale-unlimited/declaration-strict-value` comment, but the comment must state why — reviewers should treat an unexplained disable as a rejection, not a pass.
